rows.label: time to first content, cold (first bubble of a pass)
rows.title: host creation → the first size report with content, for the first boot of each pass (one sample per pass: median / p90 across passes)

rows.label: time to first content, warm
rows.title: host creation → first content for every boot after the first one of the pass

rows.label: blank while visible
rows.title: how long a bubble sat inside the viewport without content, per boot (0 = content was there before the reader got to it); boots that never got content count their whole visible time

rows.label: bubbles blank > 100 ms
rows.title: boots whose visible-without-content time exceeded 100 ms, per pass

rows.label: renderer create → first report
rows.title: the renderer alone: its construction → its first message to the host (iframe: the srcdoc document load + renderer bundle, then the first size report; shadow: the first size report, synchronous; canvas: `ready` after the wasm instance, cached after the first)

rows.label: host constructor (main thread)
rows.title: the synchronous cost of `new WidgetHost` on the main thread: renderer element, validator, worker handoff

rows.label: memory per live bubble, browser processes
rows.title: the memory ramp at the end of each pass: the drop distance is lifted and the feed is scrolled through once more so every bubble boots and stays live; (resident memory of every Chromium process with all bubbles live − with the keep window live) ÷ the bubbles added. Read by the Playwright driver (scripts/feed-report.ts); n/a in a plain tab

rows.label: memory per live bubble, page JS heap
rows.title: the same ramp on performance.memory (the main thread's V8 heap: not the workers, not an isolated frame's heap), after gc() where the browser exposes it; n/a without performance.memory

rows.label: QuickJS heap per live bubble
rows.title: the engine's own counter (memory_used_size) summed over the live widgets ÷ live widgets, at the ramp's reading with every bubble live

rows.label: live bubbles at the memory reading
rows.title: hosts alive at the ramp's reading (every bubble of the feed when the ramp completed)

rows.label: long tasks, total
rows.title: PerformanceObserver longtask (≥ 50 ms) on the main thread during the scripted scroll, summed per pass

rows.label: long-task time per second of scroll
rows.title: the total above ÷ the seconds the scripted scroll took (comparable to the iOS hitch rate in spirit, not in definition)

rows.label: longest task
rows.title: the longest single long task during the scroll

rows.label: longest frame
rows.title: the longest interval between two requestAnimationFrame callbacks during the scroll

rows.label: dropped frames (estimate)
rows.title: Σ round(interval ÷ expected) − 1 over the frames of the scroll; expected = the 20th-percentile interval of the pass (the display's refresh)

notMeasured: memory: performance.memory is the main thread's JS heap only (no workers, no isolated frame); measureUserAgentSpecificMemory is refused by this Chromium (the note under the table says so when it is); the process row is resident memory (shared pages counted once per process) over a ramp of ~1 minute: the browser's own drift over that minute is in it, the pool's warm workers are not
the pool's prewarm itself (N worker boots before the feed opens) is outside every clock
cold cache: wasm modules and the dev server's files are fetched once per page load, so only the first pass of a canvas renderer pays the fetch + compile
a background tab: Chromium throttles timers and frames there; run with the tab in front
CPU frequency, thermal state, other tabs and processes; the dev build (Vite, unminified)
the iOS report's hitch rate: long tasks start at 50 ms, so shorter main-thread stalls show only in the frame rows
